cases.case_name: The Telangana State Waqf Board vs M/S. Solithro Private Limited
cases.citation: Writ Appeal No. 1432 of 2016 (with W.P. No. 23242 of 2008)
cases.property_involved: Lands notified as Waqf in Survey Nos. 136, 137, 227 and 228, Shabhaspally village, and land in Sikindlapur Village, Shivampet Mandal
cases.location: Narsapur and Siddipet Taluks, Medak District, Telangana
cases.dispute_summary: Telangana State Waqf Board appealed a single judge order that quashed a 2001 notification declaring these lands as Waqf property, after Solithro Private Limited purchased the land at a bank auction in 2013-14. The company argued the 2001 notification was issued under the repealed 1954 Wakf Act and was therefore void.
cases.outcome_status: Court sided with the purchaser; the 2001 Waqf notification was quashed as void (issued under repealed law), and revenue authorities were directed to decide ownership afresh, effectively de-notifying the land as Waqf.

cases.case_name: M/S Sai Pawan Estates Pvt. Ltd. vs The Telangana State Wakf Board
cases.property_involved: Land in Survey No. 80, claimed as endowed to Dargah Hazrat Salar-E-Auliya
cases.location: Hafeezpet Village, Serilingampally Mandal, Ranga Reddy District
cases.dispute_summary: A three-way ownership dispute among private purchasers (claiming title via a 1958 partition decree), the State of Telangana (claiming government land per revenue records), and the Telangana State Wakf Board (claiming the land as Waqf property since 1955).
cases.outcome_status: Court rejected both the State's and the Wakf Board's claims, holding the private petitioners had valid title established over six prior rounds of litigation, and found the Wakf Board's registration lacked proper inquiry.

cases.case_name: Ghulam Samdani vs Andhra Pradesh Waqf Board, Hyderabad
cases.property_involved: Jamay Masjid, Charminar and its attached properties
cases.dispute_summary: Challenge to the Waqf Board Legal Adviser's appointment of an Official Receiver for the Charminar mosque property pending a Section 45 Wakf Act inquiry, and to the validity of Rule 10-A which purported to authorize such receiver appointments.
cases.outcome_status: Petition allowed; the receiver appointment was quashed and Rule 10-A was declared ultra vires as neither Section 44 nor Section 45 of the Wakf Act contemplated appointing a receiver pending inquiry.

cases.case_name: Sayyed Ali and Others vs Andhra Pradesh Wakf Board, Hyderabad and Others
cases.property_involved: Syed Ali Ishaq Madina Vali Dargah lands (Title Deed No. 42)
cases.location: Devada Mokhasa village, Visakhapatnam District, Andhra Pradesh
cases.dispute_summary: The Wakf Board sued in 1967 to cancel long-term leases/sub-leases granted by mutawallis without authority and to recover possession, arguing the land was a Waqf (service inam) dedicated to the Dargah; sub-lessees argued it was a personal grant to named individuals, not Waqf.
cases.outcome_status: Supreme Court upheld the High Court and Wakf Board's position, applying the principle 'once a wakf, always a wakf,' and decreed the suit in the Board's favor.

cases.case_name: Syed Masood Ahmed And Another vs The A.P. State Wakf Board
cases.property_involved: Land in Sy. No. 87 (and adjoining Sy. No. 89) claimed as part of a Wakf institution
cases.location: Hameedullah Nagar, Shamshabad Mandal, Ranga Reddy District
cases.dispute_summary: The A.P. State Wakf Board sued for a perpetual injunction against alleged encroachers/purchasers, restraining construction and alienation, claiming the property was under its management as Waqf land; petitioners relied on pattadar passbooks and title deeds from private vendors.
cases.outcome_status: High Court reversed the Waqf Tribunal, finding no evidence the Board was in possession on the date of suit and dismissing the Board's suit with costs.

cases.case_name: Allauddin Charities And Zakath Wakf vs Hameed Ali And Ors.
cases.citation: O.S. No. 664 of 1999 (VII Junior Civil Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad)
cases.property_involved: Property registered as Wakf belonging to Alladin Charities and Zakath Trust (Ward No. 21, Block 21-1-1098)
cases.area: Approximately 538 sq. yards (within a larger 9,126.06 sq. yard complex)
cases.dispute_summary: Occupants claiming ownership through gift deeds and running a trust (Faizana-e-Al-Hussain Trust) were accused by the Wakf Board of being encroachers who obtained municipal building permits using fabricated documents on registered Wakf land.
cases.outcome_status: High Court held the Wakf Tribunal, not the High Court or civil court, had exclusive jurisdiction to decide the Wakf status/title dispute; directed parties to pursue statutory remedy.

cases.case_name: Inspector-Auditor, A.P. Wakf Board vs Revenue Divisional Officer-Cum-Land Acquisition Officer
cases.property_involved: Land in Survey No. 407/5 and Survey No. 400/A, dedicated to two Dargahs, acquired for house sites for weaker sections
cases.location: Kutagulla Village, Kadiri Mandal, Andhra Pradesh
cases.dispute_summary: Dispute over entitlement to land acquisition compensation between the A.P. Wakf Board, which claimed the land as registered Wakf property, and private claimants who said their family had purchased and possessed the land since 1941, predating the Wakf dedication.
cases.outcome_status: Appeal partly allowed: claimants held entitled to compensation for Sy. No. 407/5 since the Board failed to prove dedication predated the 1941 purchase; Sy. No. 400/A matter remitted for further proceedings.

cases.case_name: Telangana State Waqf Board vs Mohamed Muzafar
cases.property_involved: Graveyard 'Mir Rahmat Ali Shah' (Muntakhab No. 998) including an occupied tenancy portion and an encroached portion
cases.area: 998.66 sq. yards total; Schedule A 90.16 sq. yards, Schedule B (encroached) 40 sq. yards
cases.dispute_summary: Waqf Board alleged the respondent was an unlawful occupant — a defaulting tenant on part of the graveyard land and an encroacher on another part — while the respondent disputed the Waqf status and the gazette notification's expanded area.
cases.outcome_status: Supreme Court upheld the Waqf Tribunal's finding that the properties were legitimate Waqf property; respondent given three months to vacate and pay rent arrears.

cases.case_name: Mohammed Azeem Khan vs Telangana State Waqf Board
cases.property_involved: Dargah Hazrat Syed Saadullah Hussaini, Badapahad - offerings/tender rights
cases.dispute_summary: Dispute over award of a sealed tender for collection of offerings at the Dargah after the highest bidder deposited funds one day after the stipulated deadline; the second-highest bidder challenged the award as improper.
cases.outcome_status: Petition dismissed; court held the deposit was timely given intervening bank holidays, and the tender award to the highest bidder stood.

cases.case_name: Telangana State Waqf Board vs The State Of Telangana
cases.property_involved: Property No. 3-3-844, notified as Waqf under A.P. Gazette dated 12.07.1984, occupied by long-term tenants
cases.dispute_summary: Waqf Board challenged a 2002 Lok Adalat award that had settled a specific performance suit for sale of the property between private parties, arguing the sale agreement was void because the land was Waqf property and the seller had no authority to alienate it.
cases.outcome_status: Writ petition dismissed on grounds of 21-year delay/laches in challenging the award despite the Board's knowledge since 2002.

cases.case_name: Syed Raza Aman And 5 Others vs The Telangana State Waqf Board And 9 Others
cases.property_involved: Ibadat Khana-e-Hussaini (IKH), a Waqf religious institution established via Waqf Deed dated 30 February 1953 (Municipal Nos. 22-2-638 to 643)
cases.dispute_summary: Internal dispute between two Shia sects (Akhbari and Usuli) over control of the prayer facility and the Managing Committee's authority to require an application form for religious functions such as Majlis-e-Aza.
cases.outcome_status: High Court partly reversed the Tribunal's injunction, allowing the Managing Committee to continue requiring the application form while upholding a restriction on removing photographs.

cases.case_name: Mushke Srinivas Reddy vs The Telangana State Waqf Board
cases.property_involved: Property in Survey No. 15, House No. 3-9, declared Waqf via a 1990 Gazette Notification
cases.location: Gudur Village, Bibinagar Mandal, Nalgonda District
cases.dispute_summary: Purchasers holding 2013 sale deeds discovered the property had been notified as Waqf land in 1990 and challenged the notification's validity, alleging procedural defects and lack of notice to prior owners, amid pending eviction proceedings by the Board.
cases.outcome_status: Court modified the lower order, granting the purchasers liberty to pursue an alternative remedy/forum for the factual dispute rather than compelling them into the pending eviction proceedings; no opinion expressed on merits.

cases.case_name: Syeda Kaneezesakina Moosavi vs Telangana State Waqf Board & Others
cases.property_involved: Bargah-e-Hazrath-e-Abbas (AS) Waqf institution, including a 'Ladies Room' occupied for 55 years
cases.area: Institution spans 1,344 square yards; Ladies Room 120 square feet
cases.dispute_summary: Dispute over appointment of Mutawalli (trustee) to a roughly 450-year-old Waqf institution, involving hereditary succession rights from a 1983 judgment, whether a female heir could hold the post, and the petitioner's alleged unlawful eviction from a residential room within the institution.
cases.outcome_status: High Court dismissed revision petitions, upholding the Tribunal's order for Mutawalli appointment under the correct statutory provision with a one-year tenure, respecting 1983 hereditary succession guidelines.

cases.case_name: M. Govinda Rao And Ors. vs A.P. State Wakf Board And Ors.
cases.property_involved: Qazi Service Inam Wakf lands, Survey Nos. 201-203/2
cases.location: Nidamanuru Village, Krishna District, Andhra Pradesh
cases.dispute_summary: Challenge to a government order permitting sale of Wakf land to tenant-occupants at Rs. 6 lakh/acre, far below an estimated market value of Rs. 30-40 lakh/acre, bypassing the Wakf Act's mandatory public auction requirement.
cases.outcome_status: Court declared the government order illegal for bypassing Section 51's mandatory public auction requirement, upheld cancellation of the sale, and directed refund with interest to the buyers.

cases.case_name: Shaik Madhar Saheb vs The State Of Telangana
cases.property_involved: Wakf land endowed for a Muslim Maternity Hospital, Survey Nos. 231, 242, 252, 256, 258-269, 280, 281, 450, 451, 457-459, 463, 469, 486, 487, 581
cases.area: Approximately 428 acres (12-16 acres allegedly sold without authorization), valued over Rs. 1000 crores
cases.dispute_summary: Former CEO of A.P. State Wakf Board challenged pending disciplinary proceedings against him for allegedly misusing his office to facilitate unauthorized alienation of Wakf land by a caretaker body (Jamat-e-Islami Social Service) that had no authority to sell the property.
cases.outcome_status: High Court upheld the disciplinary proceedings as validly initiated before the petitioner's retirement and directed their completion within four months; provisional pension continues meanwhile.

cases.case_name: Madrasa Ahle Sunnath Bahrul Uloon vs State Of Andhra Pradesh And Ors.
cases.property_involved: Wakf land dedicated to Dargah Hazrath Syed Ali Ishaq Madina Vali, and land adjacent to Haj House
cases.location: Devada Village, Visakhapatnam District (compensation land); Haj House, Hyderabad (H.No. 5-9-98)
cases.dispute_summary: Petitioner challenged a government order transferring Rs. 6.63 crore in compensation (received from alienation of the Dargah's Wakf land) from Visakhapatnam to Hyderabad to fund land acquisition for Haj House parking, alleging diversion of Dargah-specific funds.
cases.outcome_status: Petition dismissed for lack of standing; court found the funds belonged to the Wakf Board generally (not the Dargah specifically) and their use for Haj facilities was a legitimate welfare purpose.

cases.case_name: Charminar Educational Society vs State Of Telangana
cases.property_involved: Agricultural land in Survey Nos. 91 and 92, leased from the Waqf Board to an educational institution
cases.location: Mamidipally Village, Balapur Mandal, Ranga Reddy District
cases.dispute_summary: Educational society sought a court direction compelling the (newly reconstituted) Telangana Waqf Board to decide its pending lease renewal application after it had cleared outstanding lease dues per an earlier court order.
cases.outcome_status: Court directed the Waqf Board to examine the renewal application under the Waqf Properties Lease Rules, 2014 and decide promptly, with the institution's operations to continue uninterrupted meanwhile; petition disposed of without costs.
